sections.content: How many people are "construction project managers and related professionals"?

61,180 people

were counted on the census as "construction project managers and related professionals" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Construction project managers and related professionals manage and oversee major construction and civil engineering projects and major building contracts for quality of work, safety, timeliness and completion within budget. They may also forecast travel patterns and develop strategies for managing the impact of traffic-related demand.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "construction project managers and related professionals" there were more men than women (89% compared with 11%).

This means "construction project managers and related professionals" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business, media and public service professionals".

Men made up 89% and women made up 11% of "construction project managers and related professionals"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "construction project managers and related professionals" included:

  • electronics engineers
  • fire service officers (watch manager and below)
  • vehicle valeters and cleaners

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 35 to 39 years. Of the whole working population 11.5% were aged 35 to 39 years. For people working as "construction project managers and related professionals", 14.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "construction project managers and related professionals" was 16 to 19 years.

We can look at who worked as "construction project managers and related professionals" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "construction project managers and related professionals" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "construction project managers and related professionals", 5.9% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (94.5% compared with 5.5%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (86%) than self-employed (14%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
